title: Leasing Standards for Safe Deposit Boxes: Minimum Age, Reservation Priority and Holding Limits
content:
The standards a prospective lessee of Safe Deposit Boxes is measured against are the minimum age, the order in which waitlisted customers are offered boxes, the hold placed on an offered box, and the number of rentals and reservations one customer may hold.

| Standard | Value, all sizes |
| --- | --- |
| Youngest age in whole years at which a customer may lease a box | 18 |
| Order in which waitlisted customers are offered boxes | by reservation date |
| Calendar days an offered box is held for a waitlisted customer | 10 |
| Most open reservations one customer may hold | 2 |

## Rentals of one size

The number of rentals of a single size one customer may hold, reservations included, is set by that size.

| Size | Most rentals of this size held by one customer |
| --- | --- |
| 3x5 Safe Deposit Box | 2 |
| 3x10 Safe Deposit Box | 2 |
| 5x10 Safe Deposit Box | 2 |
| 10x10 Safe Deposit Box | 1 |
| 10x15 Safe Deposit Box | 1 |
| 10x20 Safe Deposit Box | 1 |

Read across the schedule, the three smaller sizes each admit two rentals by the same customer and the three larger sizes admit one apiece; the figure counts reservations as well as leases in force, so a reservation standing against a size occupies one of that size's places.

**The hold on an offered box.** The 10 calendar days are a property of the offer, not of the size, so an offered 3x5 Safe Deposit Box and an offered 10x20 Safe Deposit Box are held for the same number of days.
